blocks.h2: Getting Your Home Ready for Winter
blocks.body: In the fall, shut off and drain outdoor faucets from the inside valve, and disconnect garden hoses. Insulate pipes in the garage, crawl space and any outside walls you can reach. Seal gaps where cold air gets in near pipes. When a deep freeze is coming, keep the heat steady, even at night, and open cabinet doors on outside walls. If you're traveling, don't turn the heat down too far, and ask someone to check on the house.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.q: How do I keep pipes from freezing?
items.preview: Heat, open cabinets and a slow drip.
items.answer: Keep the heat up, open cabinets on outside walls and let a faucet drip on the coldest nights.

items.q: Can I thaw a frozen pipe myself?
items.answer: Gently with a hair dryer or warm towels. Never use an open flame.

items.q: Can you repair a pipe inside a wall?
items.answer: Yes. We locate the break and open only what's needed.

items.q: Should I leave the heat on when I travel in winter?
items.answer: Yes. Keep it at a steady setting, and have someone check on the house if you're gone long.

items.q: Can a burst pipe in the garage wall damage the house?
items.preview: Yes, if water runs into the wall.
items.answer: Yes. Water can run inside the shared wall into the house. Shut off the main and call us.

items.q: How much does burst pipe repair cost in Hanover Park?
items.preview: It depends on the break. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the pipe burst and how we reach it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
